title: Introduction to Regular Expressions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of introduction to regular expressions in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply introduction to regular expressions in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to common text-matching use cases and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Introduction to Regular Expressions through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding introduction to regular expressions helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Introduction to Regular Expressions helps you reason about ruby regex literals. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Ruby regex literals. Then connect it to Creating Regexp objects. The remaining syllabus points—Common text-matching use cases—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for introduction to regular expressions using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Common text-matching use cases), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain introduction to regular expressions, identify its place in regular expressions, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
